answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks via memory-hard proofs: each agent must maintain an 8 GB scratchpad derived from its unique cipher key and answer random byte probes within 200 ms. Storing slices on slow umber disks fails the latency deadline, so RAM cannot be compressed or deduplicated across identities. A farmer spawning a lotus swarm of 1,000 clones must run 8 TB of active RAM at $1,200/mo, yet each identity caps epoch earnings at $0.40 ($400 total). This $800 monthly deficit makes multiplying compliant identities strictly unprofitable.
